decisions.summary: when a piece fails the placer's lines, the grave cut's re-hold first cuts every convex point under 25 deg off square to its bisector (blunt_points(q, _TOE_MIN_APEX)). It keeps the piece if held_faults then passes it, instead of dropping a whole 2,179 px2 basin bare
decisions.why: This repairs a regression from wave 78 (XIII), using the form 0005's page states: 'a point the maps refuse is cut off into a headland'. Dropping a whole basin bare matches no form on that page. Round 2 confirmed it in the diff: the call site passes _TOE_MIN_APEX and nothing else, and the 14 tests in tests/waterfields/test_ring_guarantees.py pass (make test-file, this round).

decisions.summary: the headland is cut where the basin is HEADLAND_PX (4 px) across. The width is claimed UNRESEARCHED
decisions.why: 0005 names the headland but gives it no width, and a cut needs some width. An honestly UNRESEARCHED value is outside the accepted 565 findings. Wave 80's hairpin margin is the precedent.

decisions.id: W82-c cut off the drain, cut before take-in
decisions.summary: a refused point is cut into a headland at the grave corner, although 0005 puts the headland along the drain, and the cut comes before the whole piece goes to the weld. The spec row classes this as this project's GUESS, recorded on 0005's drawing page as a DEVIATION
decisions.why: Round 1's ruling stands, now with the needle floor gone. (1) A grave corner has no drain, so 'along the drain' is physically impossible there. The bullet itself rests on an absence note (note 7), so no source is departed from. (2) The page gives the cut for a POINT and the take-in for 'the odd corner'. The code's weld merges a whole piece, so cutting the point first and welding what is left applies each form to its own object. (3) The literal alternative measured in wave 82, a whole basin left bare, contradicts the page more than the cut does. Raise this with the GM at the wave's end.

decisions.summary: round 1's NOT LEGITIMATE needle floor is gone: blunt_points takes (poly, min_deg) only, a needle is cut like any other point, and held_faults decides. W18's spike test now expects the point cut off, the basin kept and its neighbor untouched. The needle clause is off 0005's page, and no 'needle not blunted' claim remains
decisions.why: Confirmed in the diff. close.py has no floor_deg or NEEDLE_DEG reference and no needle-exempt claim. test_a_needle_has_its_point_cut_off_and_its_neighbor_is_left_as_it_was asserts that the kept ring is not a needle and that held_faults is empty, and it passes this round. The page's new sentence carries no needle carve-out. The change now does what the page says, with no exception.

decisions.summary: polder.py::unpoint_parcels#pointed parcel left as bank is relabeled UNRESEARCHED, with the code unchanged
decisions.why: impl-drift named UNRESEARCHED as the correct label: 0005's bare strip is a fan's, and polder plots stand apart. This is an E0 correction under FR-003.

decisions.summary: the docstring names the grave cut as its one caller
decisions.why: A stale statement is corrected and no behavior changes. Round 1 confirmed the only call site is settlement/fields/features.py:153.

decisions.summary: PLOT_SIZES#paddy plot size, re-judged NEEDS-RESEARCH, is filed in audit/found-wave77.jsonl at E4
decisions.why: The spec's Edge Cases tier a NEEDS-RESEARCH finding E4, and the found row now does. The row is ranked, so nothing is deferred. One gap remains, reported with the spec findings rather than as a plan narrowing: ranking.json and ranking.md were not regenerated from the found row by audit/merge.py, so the committed ranking still lists the row as E1, row 11 of E1.
